summary: Aloysius Pieris was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied under Bernard de Give, at Sacred Heart College, University of London, and Pontifical Theological Faculty of Southern Italy, earning doctorates from Sri Lanka and Tilburg. He founded and directed the Tulana Research Centre.
Alubomulle Sumanasara is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Komazawa University under Yasuaki Nara.

Alva Noë is a philosopher who studied at the University of Oxford and Harvard University. He held faculty posts at the University of California, Santa Cruz (circa 1996–2003), University of California, Berkeley (circa 2003), and the City University of New York (circa 2010–2011).

Alvappillai Veluppillai was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under K. Kanapathypillai at the University of Peradeniya and Thomas Burrow at the University of Oxford. He taught at Peradeniya, Jaffna, Uppsala, and Arizona State University.

Amalananda Ghosh was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at University College London. He served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1937–1968), as a UNESCO consultant (1968–1970), and as a Fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study.
Amalia Pezzali is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under T. R. V. Murti and Michel Hulin.

Amanda K. Goodman is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who earned her Ph.D. at the University of California, Berkeley, under Robert H. Sharf, Luis O. Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez Jr. She holds a teaching position at the University of Toronto.

Amar Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Anthony Kennedy Warder and teachers Rahul Sankrityayan, Bimal Krishna Matilal, T. Venkatacharya, and Alasdair Urquhart.

Amaranatha Jha was an Indologist educated at Muir Central College. He served as Professor of English at Muir Central College, Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad (circa 1938–1946), and Vice-Chancellor of Banaras Hindu University (circa 1947–1948).

Amartya Sen is a philosopher and economist educated at the University of Calcutta and the University of Cambridge. He held academic posts at Jadavpur University, University of Delhi, the London School of Economics, and Harvard University.

Amber D. Carpenter is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under M. M. McCabe and Verity Harte, among others. Her career includes posts at the University of York, Einstein Forum, and an associate professorship at Yale-NUS College.

Amelia Hall is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford. In 2019, she was attested as Assistant Professor of Indo-Tibetan Buddhism at Naropa University and online faculty at Central Michigan University.

Amin Sweeney was a linguistics scholar who completed a doctorate at the University of London. He taught at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (1970–1977) and chaired South and Southeast Asian Studies at the University of California, Berkeley, in 1998.
Amita Chatterjee is an Indology and philosophy scholar who served as a professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University, attested in 1999 and 2009.
Amod Jayant Lele is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned a Ph.D. at Harvard University under the supervision of Parimal G. Patil.

Amy Heller is a Tibetologist and historian who earned her Ph.D. from the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Ariane Macdonald. She has held posts at the CNRS, Sapienza University of Rome, SOAS University of London, and INALCO.

Amy Paris Langenberg is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology who completed her Ph.D. at Columbia University and became an assistant professor of religious studies at Eckerd College circa 2014.

Amy Sims Miller is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her B.A. from Wesleyan University and her M.A. and Ph.D. from the University of Virginia, where she studied under David Germano and several traditional Tibetan teachers.
Amy Snyder Ohta is a scholar of linguistics and Japanology who studied at the University of California, Los Angeles, and held a post at the University of Washington around 1995.

Ana Agud is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Salamanca and the University of Tübingen. Around 1984, she became a professor in the Department of Classical and Indo-European Philology at the University of Salamanca.
